## Why

Follow-up of S618 (run ork-20261126-021911-97a7). Every real relay diff holds `.slicer/` tracking files and `landed-changed/ID.md`. The per-file `git show` list S618 added to the Base overlays section therefore fills with tracking paths up to its 20-path cap. This slice drops those paths from the changed-file split in `baseOverlaySection` (`internal/engine/baseoverlay.go:50-57`), before the cap and before the "section is nil" test, the way adj 600 does for the no-renders rule (`onlyTUITestFiles`, `internal/engine/states.go:864`). A path is skipped when it starts with `.slicer/` or `landed-changed/`, as the slice title and adj 600 say. `trackingPath` (`internal/engine/landdirty.go:86`) is narrower: it keeps `.slicer/config.json` and `.slicer/relay-roles.json`, and it does not know `landed-changed/`. A diff that holds only tracking paths gets no section.

Owner decision, 2026-11-26 (key `base-overlays.tracking-paths`, adj 610): land S618 as specced and file this follow-up (Jon chose 'Follow-up').

This slice also covers S628 (adj 611), as Jon chose 'Two slices' (session 8d711f67, 2026-11-27). A reviewer who reverts `internal/engine/brief.go` is offered only `./internal/engine`, although the new test may live in `./internal/cli`, which imports engine; the same overlay file works for that package. Owner decision (key `base-overlays.importer-packages`, adj 617): ork runs `go -C WORKTREE list` for the module's packages and adds one overlay test command per package that directly imports the reverted file's package (test imports included), each vetted by `overlayBuildError`.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-27: adj 604 (tracking paths skipped; 20-path cap), adj 617 (direct importers via go list, each vetted) and adj 625 (cap importer lines at 20 per section with a left-out line). S628 (adj 611) is merged here.

Owner decision, 2026-11-27: adj 627 (every overlay go test command carries -count=1) is folded into this slice.

All tests are in `internal/engine/baseoverlay_test.go`. The importer tests add a route for `go -C W list -e -json ./...` whose Stdout is concatenated `go list -json` objects with `ImportPath`, `Module.Path`, `Imports`, `TestImports` and `XTestImports`.

## Implement

1. In `baseOverlaySection` (`internal/engine/baseoverlay.go`), skip a changed path in the split loop (lines 51-57) when `baseOverlayTrackingPath(p)` is true. Add that helper in the same file: `strings.HasPrefix(p, ".slicer/") || strings.HasPrefix(p, "landed-changed/")`. This is the rule of `onlyTUITestFiles` (adj 600); it is not `trackingPath`, because the title and adj 600 skip every `.slicer/` path. The skip comes before the sort, so the 20-path cap, the left-out count, the nil return at line 62 and the "overlays cover non-test Go files only" paragraph all see only the remaining paths.
2. Add `baseOverlayImporters(ctx, rec) (map[string][]string, error)` in `internal/engine/baseoverlay.go`. It runs `e.d.goBin() -C WORKTREE list -e -json ./...` with `clirun.Run` and `baseOverlayVetTimeout`, and decodes the concatenated JSON objects with `json.NewDecoder` (fields `ImportPath`, `Module.Path`, `Imports`, `TestImports`, `XTestImports`).
   - For each package with a `Module`, its package argument is `.` when `ImportPath` equals `Module.Path`, else `"./" + strings.TrimPrefix(ImportPath, Module.Path+"/")`. This is the same form `packageArg(p)` gives.
   - The result maps each package argument to the sorted, deduplicated package arguments of the other module packages that list it in `Imports`, `TestImports` or `XTestImports`. A package is never its own importer.
   - A non-zero exit, a timeout or invalid JSON returns an error.
3. In `baseOverlaySection`, after the single-file loop (line 101), when `commands > 0`, call `baseOverlayImporters` once. For each Go file whose own entry offered a test command (not a `does not build` entry), take the importers of `packageArg(p)` and, for each, run `e.overlayBuildError(ctx, rec, overlayFile, importerPkg)` with that file's `overlay-N.json`.
   - No error gives ``- Importer `PKG` of `P`: `go -C WORKTREE test -overlay OVERLAY PKG` ``, with ShellWord on the worktree, overlay and package, as for the Go entries.
   - A build message gives ``- Importer `PKG` of `P`: does not build: MESSAGE.`` with no command.
   - Start these lines with `- Importer`, not ``- ` ``, so the Go entry count stays the Go files only, as for `- Other file`.
   - Apply the importer limit the owner chose (see Owner needed) to the importer lines, in file order and then package order.
4. When `baseOverlayImporters` returns an error, add one notice to the body: "Check incomplete: the packages that import the reverted files could not be listed, so only each file's own package is offered." The notice sits with the other incomplete notices and never pauses the run. When no overlay offers a command, `go list` is not called.
5. Write the importer lines in the body directly after the Go entries and before the Go left-out line. The existing intro, which says each command runs one package's tests with only that file reverted, stays as is.
6. In `internal/engine/harness_test.go`, add the default route `{Tool: "go", Args: []string{"-C", W, "list"}, Prefix: true}` (empty Stdout, exit 0) beside the `vet` route at line 336, so tests with no importer route see no importers and no notice.
7. In `internal/engine/baseoverlay_test.go`, add the `baseOverlayVetCalls` helper, update the four existing tests under Failing tests, and add the new tests.
8. In `docs/design.md`, update the Base overlays entry (lines 2071-2118):
   - say the other-file list and the section test skip every path under `.slicer/` or `landed-changed/` (S620, adj 600, adj 610);
   - say that when at least one single-file test command remains, ork runs `go -C WORKTREE list -e -json ./...` once and adds a vetted `- Importer` command for each direct importer package of the reverted file's package, test imports included, using the same overlay file, with the owner's limit and a notice when the list cannot be read (S628, adj 611, adj 617).
9. Run the Check commands below.

10. Add `-count=1` to every go test -overlay command the Base overlays section writes (per-file, all-files, importer-package and the S622 test runs), so a revert run is never served from the test cache, and update the tests that assert the command text (adj 627, folded here by the owner on 2026-11-27).
